acceptance.given: A non-empty Consumer Manifest and its applicable route transitions are defined for the toolchain replay workflow.

oracle.expected: The manifest evidence records every applicable route transition as completed for every entry, with no skipped applicable transition.
forbidden: Any applicable route transition is incomplete or skipped.
The manifest is empty or entries are omitted from reconciliation.
oracle.observable: Manifest transition-completion records and bidirectional reconciliation against repository VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing callers are inspected during route-transition verification.

acceptance.then: The verification reports 100% completion of all applicable route transitions and confirms the manifest remains non-empty and reconciled.
acceptance.when: Execute each applicable route transition and inspect the resulting Consumer Manifest evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a non-empty Consumer Manifest case with an omitted or incomplete applicable route transition and assert the completeness and reconciliation check fails.

affected_subjects: VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing repository callers
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require a complete non-empty Consumer Manifest reconciled bidirectionally with the repository real-call surface, then complete every applicable route transition and verify Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing manifest schema fields and route behavior; rollback restores prior baseline evidence without deleting historical bytes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Manifest entries transition from declared/applicable to completed for every applicable route, followed by rollback baseline observation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Verification terminates only when every non-empty manifest entry has all applicable transitions marked complete, bidirectional caller reconciliation passes, and rollback observes the prior behavior baseline.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution is configured with bounded time and output budgets.

oracle.expected: The aggregate execution record contains a deterministic terminal state derived from the execution and budget outcome.
forbidden: The aggregate hangs without a terminal state.
Equivalent executions produce unexplained different terminal states.
oracle.observable: Aggregate execution records and repeated-run comparison are inspected after the aggregate execution phase.

acceptance.then: The aggregate reaches a bounded, deterministic terminal state; budget exhaustion is represented as unsuccessful rather than indeterminate.
acceptance.when: Run the aggregate to termination, including budget exhaustion handling, and repeat an equivalent execution for deterministic comparison.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an aggregate execution that hangs, exceeds its budget without a terminal marker, or returns nondeterministic terminal states across equivalent runs.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure aggregate execution enforces bounded time/output and records a deterministic terminal state, including unsuccessful budget exhaustion, consistently across equivalent runs.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing process result schema and classify budget exhaustion as unsuccessful without changing historical evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Aggregate moves from executing to a terminal success or unsuccessful-budget state with deterministic status and bounded output.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate record has a terminal state before timeout, output budget, or process completion returns; equivalent inputs yield the same terminal classification.

acceptance.given: Historical bytes exist in the pre-repair repository state and a repair or recompilation is about to run.

oracle.expected: A byte-for-byte before/after comparison shows historical bytes are identical, while any new repair evidence is append-only and non-authorizing.
forbidden: Historical bytes are modified, rewritten, or corrupted.
Historical evidence is used as authorization for the repair.
oracle.observable: Hash and byte comparisons of the frozen historical artifact set are inspected before and after repair.

acceptance.then: The comparison passes with identical historical bytes and only append-only repair evidence is present.
acceptance.when: Capture the pre-repair byte set, perform repair, then compare every historical artifact byte-for-byte in the post-repair state.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a repair that rewrites or corrupts one frozen historical artifact byte and assert the before/after integrity check fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make repair verification preserve historical artifact bytes exactly and constrain new evidence to append-only, non-authorizing records.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No historical artifact rewrite or deletion; rollback restores only newly appended repair evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Historical artifact set is snapshotted, repair executes, then the same bytes and tracked membership remain unchanged.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All frozen historical artifact hashes and bytes match pre-repair values and any repair evidence is appended without authorizing changes.

acceptance.given: Stable and Candidate executions are being prepared for each Matrix Case with per-case fixture/state assignments.

oracle.expected: Each Matrix Case execution record assigns distinct fixture/state identities to Stable and Candidate, and the assignments are attributable to that case.
forbidden: Stable and Candidate share identical fixture/state where distinctness is required.
A Matrix Case lacks distinct fixture or state assignments.
oracle.observable: Per-case execution records are inspected for two distinct fixture/state identifiers and case attribution.

acceptance.then: All six Matrix Cases show separate Stable and Candidate fixture/state assignments in their execution evidence.
acceptance.when: Configure and execute Stable and Candidate for each Matrix Case, then inspect the per-case fixture/state records.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a Matrix Case whose Stable and Candidate records use the same fixture/state identity or omit one assignment and assert the distinctness check fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Record and validate distinct, case-attributable fixture/state assignments for Stable and Candidate in every Matrix Case.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing Matrix Case record fields compatible; add only attributable fixture/state identity validation.

slice_hint.state_transition: Each case moves from fixture preparation to Stable/Candidate execution records with distinct identities and then to validated evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All six Matrix Cases contain both Stable and Candidate records, each with a distinct fixture/state identity attributable to that case.
